headline: Ratchet & Clank moves nearly all game data into C and names more hero logic
summary: Lynder063's refactoring makes Ratchet & Clank's game data and hero logic easier to read while preserving the compiled results. PAL v2.00 remains at 100.00% matched code, with all 5,116 functions matched and 99.95% of data matched in the project's progress report. A matched function compiles to exactly the same bytes as the original game.
highlights: #219 reports 99.955% of PAL v2.00's data sections in C, with no retail numeric values committed. This measures data expressed in C, separately from the code match percentage.
Hero control modes get names at 1,532 sites (#227), and typed hero records replace raw pointer casts (#229, #230).
Shared audio voice records and real global-variable types replace duplicated layouts and address arithmetic (#216, #226, #228, #233).
Fresh-clone setup now fetches missing compilers and documents the required disc-dump steps (#221, #225).
Two compiler-matching workarounds could be removed (#231). The remaining ones stay because changing them alters the compiled code (#224).
